title: Ops Mosaic: handback and resilience sketch — week of 2027-04-11
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the on-call handback, brief incident notes, SLO signal highlights, and follow-ups for the week of 2027-04-11. Lightweight narrative for the next shift: what tripped, what we did, outstanding risks, and immediate action items. Treat as working notes — links and tickets above have canonical artifacts.

High-level summary (one-liner):
- Traffic spike + degraded KV cache hit-rate on east region caused a short-lived 99th percentile latency bump (~8 minutes) and increased tail error surface for hosted inference. Automated fallback reduced customer impact; follow-up work required on cache eviction tuning and throttling policy.

Incidents this week:
1) East region KV cache contention — Apr 11 06:13-06:21 UTC
- Symptom: sudden jump in inference 99p latency from ~220ms to ~1.5s; internal error-rate from 0.2% to 1.9%.
- Trigger: sustained burst of prefix-heavy requests from a single enterprise tenant test harness (unflagged load test) combined with a cache eviction regression introduced by small-ttl change in runtime config.
- Mitigation timeline:
  - 06:15: Scoped rate-limit applied to offending route (temporary block on tenant test key) — immediate tail reduction.
  - 06:17: Manual revert of TTL patch at runtime (hotfix) — KV hit-rate recovered over next 90s.
  - 06:20: Canary routing engaged to shift traffic to redundant shard pool while diagnostics ran.
- Impact: limited to one region; no data loss; some requests experienced timeouts and retries; one customer reported transient failed calls (support ticket #CS-1892).
- Postmortem owner: Marcus Nguyen (follow-up doc: LINKED_ARTIFACT above).

2) Intermittent auth token rotation gaps — Apr 09 morning (investigated this week)
- Symptom: sporadic 401s from background scheduler when connecting to KMS-backed key provider during a rolling rotation window.
- Root cause: rotation script assumes eventual consistency for secrets store; under certain timing windows the new key was visible but not yet propagated to all agents.
- Mitigation: short-lived fallback to cached key used; additional logging enabled.
- Action: move rotation job to coordinator-run (ticket RED-4198) and add guard checks to prevent overlapping rotations.

SLO snapshot and signals (week over week):
- Availability SLO (hosted inference overall): 99.95% target. Current week estimate: 99.93% (below target by 0.02 pts) — main contributor: east region KV latency spike.
- P99 latency (generate API): target 600ms. This week rolling p99: 720ms during incident window; baseline outside incidents 210ms.
- Error budget remaining: ~0.18% monthly (we consumed ~30% of monthly budget this interval).
- Observability notes: sampling thresholds for tracing were sufficient during the incident; however the auto-correlation between request id and shard id was missing in ~7% of traces (investigate logging pipeline).

On-call handback (for next shift):
- Current mitigation state: 1) East region shard pool patch reverted, 2) canary routing enabled and stable, 3) tenant test key blocked pending CS outreach.
- Known risk: TTL and eviction policy still on older heuristics; under heavy prefix-heavy workloads we can re-trigger similar contention.
- What to watch: KV cache hit-rate (metric: kv.cache.hit_rate) for east region < 0.85, P99 latency trending > 600ms for >1 minute, sudden spike in Replica CPU saturation > 85%.
- Escalation path: pager -> SRE lead (Dmitri Volkov) -> infra rotation -> engineering on call -> exec on-call only if customer SLOs are breached for >30 minutes.

Runbook edits (to land this week):
- Add explicit section for TTL rollback and safe-fast revert steps (owner: Marcus Nguyen, due 2027-04-15).
- Add automated detection rule to fire when a single tenant consumes >10x normal share of prefix cache insertions over 5 minutes (owner: Aisha Patel, due 2027-04-18).
- Patch auth rotation to require coordinator lock; add pre-check to reject rotation if >1% agents show older secret (owner: Lena Ortiz, due 2027-04-20).

Operational tasks and follow-ups (short list):
- RED-4123: complete post-incident analysis and memex (Marcus) — due 2027-04-18.
- RED-4160: throttle policy refinement and route-level controls (Aisha + Platform) — RFC in PR by 2027-04-22.
- Infra PR #728: runbook test harness add — validate in staging tomorrow (Dmitri) — merge window 2027-04-13.
- Observability spike: re-enable full trace sampling for 10 minutes during controlled canaries to validate correlation fields (ops-run, owner: Lena).

Meeting notes (this week's sync 2027-04-11 15:00 UTC):
- Attendees: Aisha, Marcus, Lena, Dmitri, two solutions-eng reps.
- Discussion highlights:
  - Agreed to treat tenant test harness behavior as potentially unsafe; solutions-eng to update onboarding guidelines and include a pre-flight check.
  - Decided to bake a soft quota in routing layer for onboarding tenants for the first 48 hours after key creation.
  - Prioritized runbook edits above — we have a small sprint to close the main gaps.

Customer impact and CS handoff:
- CS ticket CS-1892 opened; communicated that service was restored and we are doing a post-incident write-up. Marcus to lead customer-facing summary.
- For enterprise customers in east region, we will offer an ops review and capacity guidance if they experienced repeated thrashing. Solutions-eng to schedule.

Notes to next shift (quick checklist):
- Confirm kv.cache.hit_rate east >= 0.9 for 15m rolling window.
- Watch p99 generate API; set temporary alert threshold 650ms for next 24 hours.
- Ensure blocklist for the offending tenant test key still applied; coordinate with CS before unblocking.
- Run the debug runbook once in staging to validate TTL revert steps.

Retrospective items (to include in final postmortem):
- Hardening: automated tenant-level soft quotas, routing-based circuit breaking for prefix-heavy patterns, and improved preflight checks for test harnesses.
- Observability: ensure request->shard correlation present in every tracing span; add one-off sampling window capability.
- Process: improve cross-team communication for tenant onboarding tests; consider a lightweight gating step.

Appendix (quick links and scratch notes):
- Metric panels: grafana/dashboards/kv-cache-ops (placeholder)
- Debug command snippets (ops notes):
  - tail -f /var/log/serving-runtime/*.log | grep -i "evict"
  - curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>' https://api.redwood.internal/metrics?series=kv.cache.hit_rate&region=us-east1

If anything else is needed for handoff, ping me in #sre-ops with the prefix "ops-handback".

Quick personal note: I sketched a small canary test to surface prefix-heavy patterns earlier today — will drop the short script into infra repo under /ops/canaries and link it in the runbook PR.

— Aisha
